answer: Require each agent to post a bond that is locked until its actions survive a challenge window; if independent reviewers verify fraud, slash the bond and distribute part to challengers. One person can still create many identities, but must fund each with scarce capital and risk losing it, so multiplying fake agents becomes costly rather than free. A marble-sized bond is not enough if attackers can cheaply coordinate, so set it against expected gains; keep appeals open through the nadir of activity, not just at launch, to avoid a temporary oasis of scrutiny.
